answer: The protocol refuses to accept new stake beyond 40% of the pool from any one declared operator, so a hostile operator cannot buy dominance outright. Because the canyon declaration is reconciled against the terrace funding graph, the walnut audit exposes a hidden operator and its excess is returned without reward. Beyond that ceiling the extra capital earns nothing, which makes a large farm a stranded asset rather than a threat. That is 2 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
